title: Eager kernel validation and deterministic GPU dependency ordering
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Cold-start and nondeterministic kernel selection are causing intermittent latency spikes and increased fallback rates across heterogeneous fleets. Root causes include inconsistent .so load ordering across distros, late symbol resolution that prevents early validation of optional quantization kernels, and lack of a compact artifact manifest that encodes required vs optional symbols.

Goal: Implement a lightweight eager-validation pipeline and a deterministic dependency ordering policy so that runtime can: 1) validate the presence/compatibility of critical kernel symbols at startup within a tight time budget, 2) surface clear, actionable telemetry on missing/soft-fallback symbols, and 3) use a canonical ordering for library prelinking to eliminate flakiness between images.

Success criteria / acceptance:
- Median probe_time during warm boot reduced by >= 35% on representative hetero instances (measured via canary runs).
- Fallback_count (model variant swap) reduced by >= 50% in the first 60s after container start in canary pool.
- New validator binary (gk_validator) added to runtime image; runs within 120ms for the critical symbol set in 95th percentile.
- Deterministic manifest produced at build time and consumed by runtime to enforce prelink order.

Approach:
1) Build gk_validator: small static binary that reads a build-time symbol manifest (JSON lines) and attempts deterministic dlopen/dlsym checks for required symbols and a fast soft-check for optional symbols. Validator returns a concise status code and emits structured telemetry to the console and to telemetry endpoint.
2) Canonical manifest generation: extend the artifact pipeline to emit a canonical kernel_manifest.txt during packaging (includes SONAME, symbol list, version tags, and quantization capability flags). This lives alongside the kernel bundle.
3) Deterministic prelinking: modify entrypoint to consult kernel_manifest.txt and perform deterministic dlopen order for required libraries before spawning the main process. Use LD_PRELOAD-like behavior internal to runtime rather than global env mutation.
4) Separate optional symbol table: move quantization helpers and experimental CUTLASS bindings into a separate optional .so that the validator can check and the runtime can load lazily.
5) Telemetry & metrics: add probe_time, validated_symbols_count, missing_optional_count, deterministic_order_applied (bool) to runtime metrics. Hook into existing trace spans.
6) Tests & CI: add unit tests for manifest parsing, integration test that simulates missing optional symbol, and canary pipeline to run real containers on dedicated canary pool.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 0: internal CI and local dev images (now).
- Stage 1: canary rollout to 3 dedicated GPU instances (week 1). Monitor probe_time and fallback_count.
- Stage 2: expand to 10% of dedicated pool if metrics stable.
- Stage 3: global rollout with feature flag to disable deterministic ordering for quick rollback.

Rollback plan: Feature flag off + revert validator invocation. If live errors increase, use canary to bisect kernel bundles.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: Validator too slow on low-end recovery nodes -> mitigation: timebox to 120ms and provide a fast-path that validates only required symbols.
- Risk: Packaging changes break air-gapped upgrade flows -> mitigation: preserve backward-compatible manifest location and keep legacy probe as fallback for two releases.
- Risk: New optional .so not present in some images -> mitigation: runtime treats optional as genuinely optional and logs a clear message with remediation steps.

Backward compatibility: runtime will fall back to legacy probe if manifest absent to avoid customer-impacting failures during rollout.

2026-02-18 - Design sync: Decided on a simple native validator (gk_validator) rather than embedding validation in main process to keep failure modes isolated. Design doc uploaded.
2026-02-22 - Decision: Generate canonical manifest in packaging pipeline (runtime-artifacts job). This manifest will be stable-sorted to guarantee deterministic ordering.
2026-02-28 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345 adds kernel_manifest generator and basic validator harness. Awaiting reviews from infra and qa.

- Move quant helpers to optional.so suggested by design (accepted).
- Add extra telemetry tags for region and build_id (added).
